role: You are Codex operating as principal engineer, security engineer, release engineer, product architect and programme manager for this repository. Read this entire JSON file before acting. Treat every MUST contract as binding and merge-blocking.
primaryObjective: Create and then execute a contract-first, Conductor-managed, GitHub-tracked programme that migrates substack-cli-ts to a bleeding-edge mainline architecture, resolves all identified correctness/security/quality issues, matures the CLI, library and MCP server, publishes it broadly, and brings it to a defensible 1.0 with a long-term roadmap.
nonNegotiableOperatorDecisions: The first run is planning-only and must stop after a green planning PR so the plan can be reviewed before implementation.
Do not create or retain an experimental dependency lane. Bleeding-edge dependencies and relevant experimental features must live in mainline and pass normal required CI.
Use the newest maintained upstream prerelease/canary/nightly/next/beta/rc/alpha dependency where available; otherwise use newest stable. Pin exact resolved versions.
Create a canonical contract derived from this prompt and enforce it automatically.
Use Conductor phases, tracks, plans and tasks, cross-referenced bidirectionally to a native nested GitHub issue hierarchy.
Reuse existing issues and work rather than duplicating them.
Keep the project local-first, contract-first, safe for autonomous agents, and operable by one maintainer.
Do not perform exploratory live writes or claim external submissions that were not verified.
Interpret 'glamira' as Glama unless refreshed research identifies a distinct intended registry.

planOnlyAllowedChanges: canonical programme contract, schemas, traceability and planning validator
.github issue/PR templates needed to represent the plan
GitHub issues, native subissues, project metadata and planning PR metadata
executionProtocol.planningPrTitle: plan: Substack CLI frontier-mainline maturity programme to 1.0
planningWorkflow: Confirm git status and record the starting SHA.
Refresh upstream facts from official sources and the repository itself.
Install/update Conductor using the current official supported mechanism and run brownfield setup.
Create the canonical contract and traceability system.
Create/update all phases, tracks, plans, metadata and task lists.
Create the nested GitHub issue hierarchy and project.
Run and watch GitHub Actions with gh pr checks --watch or the current equivalent.
Fix planning-artefact failures only; do not begin runtime implementation.
Post a planning receipt and STOP.
approvalRules: Replace <PLAN_SHA256> with the canonical plan hash emitted by the planning PR.
Verify the approval refers to the current green planning PR and current plan hash.
If the plan changed after approval, require a new approval.
implementationModeAfterApproval: Merge or rebase from the approved planning baseline according to repository policy.
Implement phase by phase and track by track using Conductor.
Use reviewable PRs, preferably one phase or independently releasable track per PR.
Do not start a dependent track until its contract dependencies and required checks are satisfied.
Watch checks to green before moving to the next implementation PR.
Update Conductor, GitHub issues, project fields, traceability and evidence in the same PR as implementation.
promptRetirement: Do not delete this file in the planning PR.
Delete it only in T11-03 after zero-gap migration into canonical systems is proven.

conductorAndGitHubRules.conductorPlugin: Use the latest official gemini-cli-extensions/conductor or its current supported Codex-compatible invocation. Preserve a brownfield repository's valid context and migrate stale legacy Conductor artefacts.

planRequirements: GitHub issue/subissue number and URL per task

githubHierarchy.programmeIssue: PROGRAM: Substack CLI frontier-mainline maturity programme to 1.0
githubHierarchy.level1: Phase issues as native subissues of the programme issue
githubHierarchy.level2: Track issues as native subissues of their phase
githubHierarchy.level3: Task issues as native subissues of their track
githubHierarchy.fallback: If native subissues are genuinely unavailable, still create every issue and maintain explicit parent/child URLs plus tasklists; record the API limitation as a blocker and upgrade to native subissues when possible.

existingIssueReuse.161: Advanced testing, contract testing, required CI and quality gaps
existingIssueReuse.162: Security, branch rulesets, repository context, Renovate and Codecov
existingIssueReuse.167: Schedule collisions, horizon and queue caps
existingIssueReuse.168: Closed revise/unschedule work that must be audited and hardened

existingPullRequestReview.176: Assess as stale Dependabot-era work; retain only if not superseded by the frontier mainline dependency migration.

validatorInvariants: Every MUST contract maps to at least one track and one verification target.
Every phase contains tracks; every track contains task issues.
Every task maps to one or more contract IDs and exactly one track.
Every GitHub issue and Conductor item is bidirectionally linked.
No item can be complete without evidence.
No exception can be active without owner, rationale, compensating control, expiry and approval reference.
No implementation may start before the approved planning hash is recorded.
No registry target may be marked published without a verified URL or API receipt.
Prompt retirement is impossible while any prompt requirement is unmapped.

selectionAlgorithm: For each direct dependency, query npm view <package> dist-tags --json, npm view <package> time --json, upstream releases, migration guides and advisories.
Prefer the maintained tag representing the newest upstream code among next, canary, nightly, dev, beta, rc and alpha; use latest only when no maintained newer channel exists.
Do not select abandoned, yanked, malicious, licence-incompatible or demonstrably unrelated tags.
Resolve the selected tag to an exact version and commit it; never store the floating tag.
If experimental functionality exists only at a Git commit, pin the exact commit and make the published artefact self-contained.
requiredMainlineTargets: Newest Node.js Current and compatible npm
TypeScript next/native compiler with parallelism controls
MCP TypeScript SDK v2 split packages and protocol 2026-07-28
MCP Tasks extension and MCP Apps extension
Zod canary or newest Standard Schema-compatible frontier validator
Hono frontier release for HTTP transport where appropriate
Current YAML and Markdown AST ecosystem
Current public-suffix and Temporal/time libraries where needed
mainlineRules: All selected dependencies live in normal dependencies/devDependencies and normal lockfile.
All selected experimental APIs are compiled and tested by required CI.
Runtime capability negotiation and safety policy are permitted; a separate test lane or branch is not.
Maintain compatibility shims only when required by an upstream transition and delete them on an explicit expiry.
Record rollback versions and migration notes for every major/frontier change.

requiredPrimaryTargets.name: npm
requiredPrimaryTargets.completion: Verified public package version with provenance

requiredPrimaryTargets.name: Official MCP Registry
requiredPrimaryTargets.completion: Published immutable version and verified registry URL

requiredPrimaryTargets.name: Glama
requiredPrimaryTargets.purpose: Maintainer-verified indexing, build, inspection and discoverability
requiredPrimaryTargets.completion: Verified Glama server page and passing build/introspection

requiredPrimaryTargets.name: Smithery
requiredPrimaryTargets.completion: Verified Smithery page using MCPB and/or Streamable HTTP as appropriate

requiredDownstreamVerification: VS Code MCP Gallery/official registry integration
additionalTargetsToAssess: mcpservers.org and other maintained directories with material discovery value
submissionRules: Refresh each registry's current official submission requirements immediately before work.
Generate metadata from the capability registry and release version.
Use account-gated actions when access exists; otherwise create an exact external-gate receipt and owner command.
Never mark a registry published from a pending submission or unverified auto-index.
Monitor listings for build, metadata, security, version and availability drift.

contracts.statement: The first Codex execution is planning-only. It may create or update programme-governance artefacts, Conductor context, the canonical contract, GitHub issues/subissues, and the planning PR, but it must not change runtime source, dependencies, lockfiles, release configuration, or live Substack state.
acceptanceCriteria: The planning PR contains no runtime feature implementation or dependency migration.
Codex stops after the planning PR is pushed and all available checks are green or a pre-existing check failure is precisely evidenced.
The final planning-stage report explicitly states that implementation has not started.
requiredEvidence: GitHub Actions check URLs and conclusions

contracts.statement: Create a canonical machine-readable implementation contract derived from this prompt and make it the binding source of truth for all subsequent work.
acceptanceCriteria: The contract records this prompt's SHA-256, every contract ID, phase, track, task, dependency decision, acceptance criterion, GitHub issue reference, Conductor path, status, evidence, and exception.
A deterministic validator fails on missing mappings, duplicate IDs, invalid states, orphaned tasks, unapproved scope changes, or completion without evidence.
Every implementation PR runs the contract validator as a required check.

contracts.statement: Represent the programme as a native GitHub issue hierarchy cross-referenced bidirectionally with Conductor.
acceptanceCriteria: One programme issue contains native phase subissues.
Each phase issue contains native track subissues.
Every track contains native task subissues for all independently verifiable tasks.
Existing issues are reused rather than duplicated and are attached to the correct parent hierarchy.
Every Conductor phase, track, and task includes the corresponding GitHub issue number and URL; every issue includes the Conductor ID and path.
requiredEvidence: GitHub Project view or reproducible project configuration

contracts.statement: Reconcile all existing issues, pull requests, branches, tracks, decisions, and partially implemented work before creating new work items.
acceptanceCriteria: Open issues #161 through #167 are mapped and reused.
Closed issue #168 and its implementation are explicitly audited against the new mutation contracts.
Open PR #176 is assessed and either incorporated, superseded with explanation, or retained with a documented dependency.
No duplicate issue or track is created for work already represented.
requiredEvidence: Issue and PR comments documenting supersession or reuse

contracts.statement: Implementation may begin only after the user explicitly approves the green planning PR using the approved plan hash.
acceptanceCriteria: The planning receipt emits a canonical plan hash.
The prompt defines the required approval phrase and Codex verifies it before implementation.
No code implementation, dependency migration, release, registry submission, or live mutation occurs before approval.
requiredEvidence: Approval-gate logic in the canonical contract

contracts.statement: Retire this prompt only after all of its content has been migrated into the canonical contract, Conductor, and GitHub issue systems with complete traceability.
acceptanceCriteria: A prompt-retirement check proves every prompt contract, phase, track, task, dependency rule, registry target, and roadmap item has an equivalent canonical record.
Deletion occurs in a dedicated final governance commit or PR and not in the initial planning PR.
The deletion receipt records the original prompt hash and replacement artefacts.

contracts.statement: Integrate the current edithatogo/repository-standards system and inherit its latest applicable node/software, supply-chain, coverage, release, verification-receipt, and solo-maintainer controls.
acceptanceCriteria: The repository is registered or refreshed in repository-standards with the correct profile and risk posture.
Centrally managed files are not forked silently; repository-owned deviations are explicit exceptions.
The one-command verification receipt conforms to the current repository-standards schema.
The model remains operable by one maintainer with zero mandatory human approvals and strong automated gates.

contracts.statement: No requirement may be removed, weakened, deferred, or reinterpreted silently.
acceptanceCriteria: Any exception contains the affected contract IDs, evidence, risk, compensating controls, expiry, owner, and explicit user approval.
Contract changes produce a new contract version and plan hash.
Codex chooses a safe best-effort implementation rather than asking avoidable clarification questions.
requiredEvidence: ADR or decision record for material changes

contracts.statement: There must be no separate experimental dependency lane, branch, package, or non-blocking workflow. Selected bleeding-edge dependencies and experimental capabilities belong to the main library and normal required CI.
acceptanceCriteria: Remove the experimental-dependency script, workflow matrix, documentation, and package scripts.
No dependency or feature is tested only in a continue-on-error lane.
All selected frontier dependencies are exact-pinned in the main package and exercised by required checks.

contracts.statement: Migrate every direct dependency to the newest maintained upstream release available at execution time, preferring an official next, canary, nightly, dev, beta, rc, or alpha channel over latest stable when such a channel exists and represents newer supported code.
acceptanceCriteria: Codex queries npm dist-tags, publication times, upstream release notes, migration guides, and security advisories at execution time.
Every direct dependency is pinned to an exact resolved version; no caret, tilde, wildcard, floating tag, or floating Git reference remains.
If no maintained prerelease exists, use the newest stable release.
If an unpublished upstream commit is required, pin an exact commit SHA, preserve licence/provenance, and bundle or vendor it so the published npm artefact installs without Git.
The package lock is regenerated and committed.

contracts.statement: Inspect every direct dependency and runtime for relevant experimental APIs, flags, transports, extensions, performance controls, and security features; adopt all relevant features in mainline.
acceptanceCriteria: The adoption manifest records package, resolved version, upstream source, experimental feature, relevance assessment, adopted implementation, tests, and rollback.
A feature may be excluded only if irrelevant, removed upstream, mutually incompatible, or demonstrably unsafe; every exclusion requires an evidence-backed contract exception.
Capability negotiation or safety policy may control runtime use, but the implementation remains present and tested in mainline.

contracts.statement: Use the newest supported Node.js Current release and newest compatible npm release as the main development, CI, build, test, and release baseline.
acceptanceCriteria: Pin the exact runtime in packageManager/devEngines and standard toolchain files.
Remove Node 18 and Node 20 support claims.
Required CI runs on the current runtime across Linux, macOS, and Windows.
Use relevant current-runtime experimental capabilities, including the permission model and configuration features, under the normal required test suite.

contracts.statement: Use the newest TypeScript next/nightly compiler as the primary compiler and type checker, including relevant native TypeScript 7 experimental parallelism controls.
acceptanceCriteria: TypeScript next is exact-pinned and is the compiler used by build and required CI.
Benchmark and configure --checkers and --builders, and retain --singleThreaded as a deterministic diagnostic mode.
Use the TypeScript 6 compatibility package only where a tool still requires the legacy programmatic API; it must not replace the primary compiler.
All removed/deprecated compiler options and type errors are resolved rather than suppressed.

contracts.statement: Replace @modelcontextprotocol/sdk v1 with the newest v2 split packages and explicitly adopt MCP protocol revision 2026-07-28 in mainline.
acceptanceCriteria: Use the official codemod as a starting point and complete the manual migration.
Use @modelcontextprotocol/server plus the appropriate Node/Hono middleware packages and Standard Schema validators.
Remove v1 imports and dead compatibility code except a deliberate dual-era transport adapter.
Adopt 2026-07-28 stateless requests, header routing, deterministic/cacheable lists, MRTR support, authorization hardening, and extensions.

contracts.statement: Keep tightly coupled dependency families on coherent versions and eliminate accidental duplicate majors.
acceptanceCriteria: All Tiptap packages resolve to one coherent frontier version unless an approved ADR documents an unavoidable split.
Vitest and its coverage provider are aligned.
MCP v2 packages and extensions are aligned.
OpenTelemetry packages are aligned.
npm dedupe and a duplicate-major policy check pass.

contracts.statement: Remove the public package's file:vendor/substack-api dependency and establish a publishable, reproducible ownership model.
acceptanceCriteria: Use an internal workspace package bundled into the tarball, ordinary internal imports, or a separately versioned package.
The clean packed artefact installs without repository-relative files or nested source-tree assumptions.
Vendored source provenance, licence, update process, and divergence are documented.

contracts.statement: Configure Renovate to track the same prerelease channels used by mainline, pin exact versions and action digests, and open normal blocking PRs rather than experimental-lane updates.
acceptanceCriteria: The inherited edithatogo Renovate preset is used where applicable.
Prerelease following is enabled for selected packages.
Automerge is limited to changes that pass the complete required suite and respect risk classification.
Dependabot is removed only after Renovate is verified healthy.
requiredEvidence: Dependency Dashboard or successful Renovate PR

contracts.statement: Parse frontmatter booleans strictly so false remains false, especially shouldSendEmail.
acceptanceCriteria: shouldSendEmail: false produces boolean false and should_send_email=false.
Quoted true/false are handled deliberately.
Invalid boolean-like values block preflight rather than coercing truthy.
Revision and republish default to no email resend.

contracts.statement: Replace synthetic HTTP status 0 and broad status heuristics with discriminated transport outcomes and operation-specific success contracts.
acceptanceCriteria: Transport results distinguish response, network-error, cancelled, timeout, and outcome-unknown.
Every operation defines allowed response codes and validates the response schema.
No network failure or redirect can be reported as success.

contracts.statement: Represent lost responses after a possible mutation as outcome-unknown and reconcile before any replay.
acceptanceCriteria: A connection loss after request transmission never becomes an automatic retry or definitive failure.
The recovery path reads remote state and resolves success, failure, or continued uncertainty.
Run logs and exit codes distinguish outcome-unknown.

contracts.statement: Retry mutations only when server-side idempotency is verified and actually transmitted, or when reconciliation proves the original mutation did not occur.
acceptanceCriteria: A local string is never treated as remote idempotency.
POST retries are disabled by default.
Idempotency keys are bound to an exact canonical plan and sent according to verified endpoint contracts.

contracts.statement: Bind credentials and cookies to verified HTTPS origins, paths, and redirect destinations.
acceptanceCriteria: Cookie headers are computed per request from a scoped cookie jar.
Substack cookies are never forwarded to arbitrary publication or redirect hosts.
Redirects are handled manually and re-authorized.
Custom domains and canonical Substack API origins are modelled separately.

contracts.statement: Distinguish authentication from authorization and require verified publication identity and role for every mutation.
acceptanceCriteria: Authenticated-but-not-authorized is a distinct failure.
Writes require a typed AuthorizedPublicationSession.
Publication ID, role, origin, and current authority are checked immediately before mutation.

contracts.statement: Enforce an explicit workspace boundary for every CLI and MCP filesystem read or write.
acceptanceCriteria: Resolve real paths and reject traversal, absolute-path escape, symlink/junction escape, UNC escape, and case-folding escape.
Only approved regular files under declared roots are accepted.
Media and fixture operations enforce size, type, and resource limits.

contracts.statement: Prohibit guessed POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE endpoint discovery.
acceptanceCriteria: Unknown mutations remain planning-only or manual.
Every executable mutation references exact first-party capture evidence, method, request schema, response schema, and last verified version.
Domain, team, refund, moderation, subscriber, publication-setting, revise, and unschedule surfaces are audited.

contracts.statement: Separate project configuration, user configuration, runtime state, cache, browser profiles, audit logs, and credentials; protect credentials with the platform credential store or an equivalent encrypted design.
acceptanceCriteria: Secrets do not live in repository-local JSON.
Files containing sensitive state use restrictive permissions and safe platform locations.
config explain identifies each value's source without revealing it.

contracts.statement: Redact and classify sensitive data structurally before any value reaches console, logs, MCP output, traces, fixtures, errors, or CI artefacts.
acceptanceCriteria: No raw arbitrary error string is persisted.
Correlation uses one-way fingerprints rather than partial secret disclosure.
Run-log privacy levels default to minimal.
Secret-scanner tests use synthetic credentials only.

contracts.statement: Maintain an evidence-backed threat model for CLI, browser, internal API, official API, MCP stdio, MCP HTTP, registry distribution, state storage, and supply-chain boundaries.
acceptanceCriteria: Threats include credential exfiltration, SSRF, prompt/argument injection, path traversal, confused deputy, replay, duplicate mutation, supply-chain compromise, PII leakage, and malicious repository content.
Each threat maps to controls, tests, residual risk, and owner.
The model is reviewed for each release.

contracts.statement: Every significant mutation must be represented by a canonical immutable machine-readable plan before execution.
acceptanceCriteria: Plans include stable action IDs, actor, publication ID, origin, content hash, request schema version, before-state expectations, expiry, risk class, reversibility, and exact intended effects.
Execution consumes the stored plan rather than reconstructing actions from free-form CLI arguments.
Canonical serialization and plan hashing are deterministic.

contracts.statement: Approval must be cryptographically or independently bound to the exact plan and must not be a self-generated unhashed checksum available to the planner.
acceptanceCriteria: Use HMAC with a key unavailable to the planner, a detached signature, or a separately persisted human approval record.
Approvals expire, are single-use, identify the approver, and reject drift or replay.
The old draft-mutation approval-token implementation is audited and replaced.

contracts.statement: A publication catalogue and scheduling-freeze policy must fail closed across every mutation path while allowing read-only inspection and planning.
acceptanceCriteria: All mutation entry points share one policy kernel.
Autonomous-agent tests prove frozen and unapproved flows make zero transport mutations.
Issue #164 is reused and completed.

contracts.statement: Verify mutation success by reading remote after-state and comparing it to the approved plan.
acceptanceCriteria: A local click, response status, or returned message alone is insufficient.
Missing, duplicate, drifted, scheduled, published, revised, or unscheduled states are reported deterministically.
Issue #166 is reused and completed.

contracts.statement: Every reversible or partially reversible mutation produces a compensating plan and recovery instructions.
acceptanceCriteria: Partial media upload, settings update, schedule, unschedule, revision, team, subscriber, and billing operations identify available compensation.
Irreversible operations are explicitly labelled and require stronger approval.
Recovery is deterministic and auditable.

contracts.statement: Unschedule and published revision preserve the canonical URL where required, default to no resend, reconcile before and after, and never use a schedule endpoint as an unschedule guess.
acceptanceCriteria: Exact captured endpoint and payload evidence exists.
keep-url and no-resend are plan-bound fields.
Issue #168 implementation is retained only if it satisfies the new contract; otherwise it is reverted or replaced.

contracts.statement: Enforce whole-publication schedule collisions, queue caps, maximum horizon, normalized spacing, IANA timezone semantics, DST ambiguity handling, and remote precision tolerances.
acceptanceCriteria: Issue #167 is reused and completed.
Property tests cover DST gaps/folds, multiple series, queue limits, and remote timestamp truncation.
All schedule and note paths use the same policy.

contracts.statement: Use the current Node built-in SQLite capability where appropriate for transactional state, durable tasks, approvals, event logs, mappings, migrations, and locks.
acceptanceCriteria: WAL, transactions, foreign keys, integrity checks, schema migrations, and crash recovery are tested.
JSON import/export remains available for portability.
The storage abstraction can be replaced without changing domain logic.

contracts.statement: Maintain an append-only tamper-evident event ledger with hash chaining, stable identities, and minimal privacy-preserving records.
acceptanceCriteria: Event hashes are verified on load and export.
Concurrency cannot lose or reorder committed events.
Audit retention and redaction policies are explicit.

contracts.statement: Treat media staging and draft mutation as one recoverable transaction.
acceptanceCriteria: Validate magic bytes, size, dimensions, type, and workspace before upload.
Deduplicate media by content hash.
Required media failure blocks the draft unless an explicitly approved degraded plan exists.
Orphaned uploads and partial failures produce recovery receipts.

contracts.statement: Publication settings updates require an approved plan and transmit only a strict allowlisted patch with before-state evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: Default library calls do not mutate.
Server-managed fields are never echoed back in a merged object.
Logo/favicon partial failures produce compensation.

contracts.statement: Use server publication IDs, stable content IDs, repository-relative paths, preserved import provenance, and efficient event hashing.
acceptanceCriteria: Absolute local paths are not exported by default.
Imports preserve immutable event IDs, timestamps, and sequences.
Cross-platform relocation and case-folding tests pass.

contracts.statement: Rate-limit policy imports may only move toward greater safety by default and cannot self-assert server provenance or confidence.
acceptanceCriteria: Imported receipts cannot shorten intervals or increase mutation retries without independently approved override.
Source and confidence are system-derived.
One parser handles all Retry-After forms using an injectable clock and RNG.

contracts.statement: Provide lossless export, import, backup, verification, restore, and rollback for local state and recoverable Substack content.
acceptanceCriteria: Backups are versioned, checksummed, portable, privacy-aware, and restorable in a clean environment.
Restore validates schema and hash chain before replacing state.
Disaster-recovery drills are automated.

contracts.statement: Refactor the monolithic CLI into a contract-first modular architecture with domain, application, adapters, and interfaces.
acceptanceCriteria: CLI registration, validation, orchestration, business logic, transports, persistence, and output formatting are separable and testable.
Simple commands do not eagerly load browser/AI dependencies.
Dependency direction is enforced automatically.

contracts.statement: Use one declarative command/capability registry to generate CLI, MCP, schemas, completions, documentation, safety classifications, and coverage metadata.
acceptanceCriteria: Each capability records ID, input/output schemas, transport, stability, evidence, read/write class, destructive/idempotent hints, approval requirement, and fallback.
Generated artefacts are drift-checked in CI.
No manual duplicate command catalogue remains.

contracts.statement: Separate official Substack API, undocumented internal creator API, browser automation, and simulator adapters with explicit support and stability labels.
acceptanceCriteria: No undifferentiated 'Substack API' abstraction hides provenance.
Every endpoint records official/internal/browser status, auth, evidence, last verification, and safety state.
Domain logic is transport-independent.

contracts.statement: Publish a stable programmatic API with explicit exports while preserving the CLI and MCP interfaces.
acceptanceCriteria: package.json has an exports map and separates executable and library entry points.
Public API compatibility tests and API-extractor or equivalent reports exist.
Internal modules are not accidentally exported.

contracts.statement: Provide predictable machine and human CLI modes, contextual completions, stable exit codes, cancellation, timeouts, config explain, and accessible help.
acceptanceCriteria: Commands support JSON/JSONL where appropriate, --quiet, --no-color, --output, and documented exit codes.
Bash, zsh, fish, and PowerShell completions are contextual and tested.
All long operations accept AbortSignal/cancellation.

contracts.statement: Replace regex-first Markdown conversion with a source-position-preserving Markdown AST mapped directly into validated ProseMirror structures.
acceptanceCriteria: Support reference links/images, escaped delimiters, nested syntax, raw HTML policy, frontmatter YAML, and source-located diagnostics.
Untrusted HTML is explicitly allowlisted/sanitized.
Round-trip and differential fixtures cover long-form Substack content.

contracts.statement: Mature the product into a safe multi-publication workspace and Creator OS while preserving local-first operation.
acceptanceCriteria: Workspace manifests, publication profiles, catalogues, calendars, campaign plans, analytics snapshots, and audit receipts use stable IDs.
Cross-publication mutation requires explicit target authority and plan binding.
Batch operations are selector-bound, resumable, and reconciled.

contracts.statement: Expand content, media, scheduling, notes, comments, analytics, backup, and publication-management features only through evidence-backed contracts.
acceptanceCriteria: Unsupported or probe-only features remain accurately labelled.
Empty valid collections are returned as successful empty results rather than schema drift.
Every feature has dry-run, reconciliation, audit, and recovery semantics appropriate to its risk.

contracts.statement: Serve MCP 2026-07-28 explicitly with the stateless core, self-describing requests, header-based routing, deterministic/cacheable catalogues, and per-request capabilities.
acceptanceCriteria: Streamable HTTP uses the official v2 handler and current Node/Hono adapter.
tools/list, resources/list, and prompts/list have deterministic order and validated cache hints.
Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name routing is tested.

contracts.statement: Provide first-class stdio and Streamable HTTP transports from the same capability registry, with deliberate legacy-era compatibility rather than duplicated servers.
acceptanceCriteria: serveStdio or its current official equivalent explicitly supports the selected protocol era.
The HTTP server is stateless and horizontally safe.
No legacy HTTP+SSE implementation is newly adopted.

contracts.statement: Implement the current MCP Tasks extension for durable long-running operations using capability negotiation and the transactional state store.
acceptanceCriteria: Task creation is durable before the handle is returned.
tasks/get, tasks/update, tasks/cancel, TTL, polling, input responses, cooperative cancellation, and recovery are tested.
Clients without task capability receive a safe ordinary result or explicit capability error.

contracts.statement: Adopt the current MCP Apps extension in mainline for safe review-oriented interfaces such as plan review, trace comparison, coverage, campaign preview, and reconciliation.
acceptanceCriteria: Apps are capability-negotiated and never required for core operation.
UI surfaces cannot bypass the common policy, approval, or workspace kernels.
Accessibility and untrusted-content isolation are tested.

contracts.statement: Implement current MCP authorization hardening for remote distribution, including issuer validation, credential isolation, scope step-up, client metadata documents, TLS, and least privilege.
acceptanceCriteria: Remote mode never shares Substack credentials across users, issuers, or publications.
Local stdio remains available without unnecessary remote auth complexity.
Smithery/hosted distribution has a documented credential model and privacy boundary.

contracts.statement: Every MCP tool has accurate readOnly, destructive, idempotent, and open-world annotations, strong descriptions, bounded schemas, and safe structured errors.
acceptanceCriteria: Annotation drift is generated from the capability registry and checked.
Glama/registry tool introspection confirms metadata.
No write tool is exposed without the common mutation contract.

contracts.statement: Produce installable npm, MCPB, Docker/OCI, stdio, and Streamable HTTP distributions from one reproducible release.
acceptanceCriteria: Clean-room installation and Inspector tests pass for every format.
Registry metadata versions match package and release versions.
No distribution includes secrets, local state, capture artefacts, or repository-relative dependencies.

contracts.statement: Build a deterministic Substack protocol simulator with fake clock, deterministic RNG, request ledger, partial failures, lost responses, retries, auth expiry, schema drift, conflicts, rate limits, redirects, and zero-mutation assertions.
acceptanceCriteria: Simulator scenarios cover every read and write capability.
No CI test requires a live Substack mutation.
Fixtures are redacted, schema-versioned, and replayable.

contracts.statement: Replace misleading headline coverage with risk-weighted assurance and remove blanket exclusions from high-risk modules.
acceptanceCriteria: Credential, authorization, policy, planning, mutation, state, media, billing, subscriber, team, and MCP HTTP code has explicit branch and mutation targets.
Coverage exclusions require contract exceptions.
Issue #161 is reused and completed.

contracts.statement: Use property-based, model-based, fuzz, mutation, differential, metamorphic, contract, concurrency, fault-injection, and snapshot testing where warranted.
acceptanceCriteria: Parsers, paths, plans, schedules, redaction, state machines, tasks, and transport recovery receive advanced testing.
Fuzz failures are minimized and retained as regression fixtures.
Mutation score thresholds are risk-specific and blocking.

contracts.statement: Provide a manual, disposable-publication canary that creates, reconciles, revises, unschedules, and cleans up uniquely identified test content without affecting production publications.
acceptanceCriteria: The canary is opt-in, account-gated, idempotent by reconciliation, and always attempts cleanup.
It cannot run on pull_request events.
It emits a redacted receipt and marks uncertain outcomes.

contracts.statement: Establish performance budgets and privacy-preserving OpenTelemetry-compatible logs, metrics, and traces for CLI, MCP, simulator, parser, state, and release operations.
acceptanceCriteria: Telemetry export is opt-in and local/no-export by default.
Benchmarks cover startup, parse, plan, catalogue, simulator, and state operations.
Regressions beyond approved budgets block merge.

contracts.statement: Provide one deterministic verification command that runs contracts, generation drift, types, lint, tests, coverage, mutation, fuzz smoke, package checks, MCP conformance, security checks, and receipt generation.
acceptanceCriteria: The command works locally and in CI.
It emits a machine-readable verification receipt conforming to repository-standards.
Release consumes the same verified artefacts rather than rebuilding differently.

contracts.statement: Run blocking checks on Linux, macOS, and Windows using the main Node Current runtime and exact package-manager version.
acceptanceCriteria: Path, permissions, shell, browser-profile, atomic-state, package-install, and completion behaviour are tested across platforms.
OneDrive/SharePoint scenarios receive dedicated Windows tests.
No obsolete Node support lane remains.
